findings.note: The "destination flags and perms" assertion cannot fail on flags. The condition is `!strings.HasSuffix(o, " "+itoa(flags)+" -rw-------") && !strings.Contains(o, "-rw-------")`; the second clause is false for every recorded open because writeFile always passes 0o600, so the `&&` short-circuits to false and the flag half of the check is inert. Proved by mutation: changing export.go:222 from `os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` to `os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL` leaves the entire export package green, so O_NOFOLLOW -- the TOCTOU defense on the final path component, the one thing checkDest's component walk cannot cover -- has zero coverage. (Changing the perm to 0o644 does fail, confirming only the perm clause is live; dropping O_EXCL is caught separately by TestOSFS:553, not by this loop.) Two further defects in the dead clause: `itoa` (export_test.go:120) reduces the flag word to a single decimal digit via `i%10`, and the literal `0x100` is darwin's O_NOFOLLOW -- on Linux it is 0x20000 -- so even if the clause were reachable it would be wrong on the CI platform.

evidence.note: if !strings.HasSuffix(o, " "+itoa(...)+" -rw-------") && !strings.Contains(o, "-rw-------")
comment claims the loop checks destination flags and perms
func itoa(i int) string { return string(rune('0' + i%10)) }

findings.note: The comment "Superseded result files are collected only once the gate has passed, so a failing run never destroys the record it was judged on" states a data-safety property that no test enforces. Removing the `if !result.Blocking` guard so packWriter.GC runs unconditionally leaves `go test ./...` green (verified over three runs in a scratchpad copy). GC deletes committed shard result files under docs/metareview/shards/, so a regression here destroys the evidence a blocking run was judged on -- precisely the outcome the comment claims is prevented. Note that the sibling housekeeping call is covered: deleting the packWriter.Prune line does fail TestTaskDonePlanIsWrittenAndPrunedWithMatchingHash, so the gap is specific to the blocking guard.

evidence.note: comment: a failing run never destroys the record it was judged on
if !result.Blocking { _ = packWriter.GC(...) } -- deleting the guard is not detected

findings.note:
The sharded-section placement invariant in reviewMarkdown is stated in a comment and enforced by nothing. The comment says the section "sits after the verdict value line, so reviewlog still reads the verdict token as the first non-empty line after the heading" -- a real contract (reviewlog.go:120 sets summary.Verdict = nextNonEmpty(lines, i+1)). Two mutations both leave `go test ./...` green: (a) rewriting line 560 as `"## Verdict

" + shardedReview + verdict + "

"`, which would make reviewlog parse the verdict as the literal string "## Sharded Review" on every run that ingested shard results; and (b) deleting `shardedReview += "

"` at line 551, which runs the last table row of the sharded section directly into the `## Reviewer Results` heading. The only direct unit test of reviewMarkdown passes "" for the new parameter (review_markdown_test.go:22), so the non-empty rendering path is executed by end-to-end tests but never asserted on.

shardedReview += "\n\n" -- deletable with no test failure

"## Verdict

" + verdict + "

" + shardedReview -- reorderable with no test failure

findings.note: The new BranchDiffFull plumbing into the reviewer context has no test. Deleting `BranchDiffFull: git.BranchDiffFull,` leaves `go test ./...` green. This is not cosmetic: reviewers/taskdone.go:350-356 falls back to the truncated `git.Diff` when BranchDiffFull is empty, so losing this line silently narrows the scan window for the eval and TODO/FIXME lints back to the truncated view -- the exact failure mode the comment at reviewers/taskdone.go:347-349 describes as having previously hidden violations by accident. The rubric blocks on both of those lints, so a silent regression here weakens the gate itself. internal/reviewers tests exercise addedLines with a synthetic GitContext and internal/gitcontext tests exercise the field's population, but nothing asserts the two are wired together in a task-done run.

branch := git.BranchDiffFull; if branch == "" { branch = git.Diff } -- silent fallback to the truncated diff

findings.note: The markedLog fixture's porcelain status is not shaped like the real producer's output, and the gap hides a live defect in statusPaths. The fixture only ever contains an ordinary porcelain-v2 entry and an untracked entry, both with space-free trailing paths, so `statusPaths` (export.go:348, "the last field of each line") always happens to be right. Against real `git status --porcelain=v2 --untracked-files=all` output -- which is what feeds TreeData.Status and the commit_exists gate detail (gate/git.go:195, gate/gates.go:121) -- it is wrong twice. Reproduced against a real repo: a rename emits `2 R. N... <hashes> R100 new_name.txt<TAB>old_name.txt` and a modified spaced path emits `1 M. N... <hashes> a file with spaces.txt`. Calling the real statusPaths on those two lines returns ["old_name.txt" "spaces.txt"] where the correct answer is ["a file with spaces.txt" "new_name.txt"]. The export bundle is described as "evidence for a reader" (export.go:2), and its tree.status, snapshot tree_status and gate detail_summary.files will name the pre-rename path and a truncated fragment of any path containing a space. The code fix belongs to shard-1f (internal/fsm/export/export.go); the missing fixture cases belong here.

evidence.note: fixture status has only space-free ordinary and untracked entries, never a rename or a spaced path
statusPaths takes strings.Fields(line)[len-1]; for a v2 rename that is the ORIGINAL path, and for a spaced path only its trailing token
git status --porcelain=v2 --untracked-files=all is the actual producer of the string statusPaths parses

findings.note: Leak marker "porcelain-file.go \n" in the must-not-appear list can never match, so it asserts nothing. Two independent reasons: the fixture at line 146 has no space before the newline, and any literal newline is escaped to the two characters backslash-n by JSON encoding before it reaches the bundle, so no marker containing a literal newline can ever be found by strings.Contains over the written files. Verified by encoding the exact fixture string: strings.Contains(json.Marshal(status), "porcelain-file.go \n") is false, and so is the same test without the stray space. The property the marker was presumably meant to guard (the raw porcelain line does not leak) is in fact covered by the tree-status shape assertion at lines 296-300 and by the diff-marker case, so this is dead weight rather than an open hole -- but it reads to a maintainer as coverage that does not exist.

evidence.note: marker list containing "porcelain-file.go \n"
the fixture the marker is supposed to match has no space before the newline
